text:
Re: Oliver Mbeki, 35

Oliver had an echo for a murmur found at an insurance medical: asymmetric septal hypertrophy 19 mm, no resting LVOT obstruction, LVEF 70%. He gets mild breathlessness only on heavy exertion such as running, with no chest pain, syncope or presyncope, and no family history of sudden death that he knows of. ECG: LVH with deep lateral T wave inversion. I have advised him to avoid competitive sport for now. I'd appreciate assessment for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, risk stratification and family screening advice.

Dr Gemma Thorne
note: Probable new HCM without high-risk features (no syncope or family sudden death); needs specialist assessment within months.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Vincent Alvarez, 66

Vincent has had 9 months of unsteadiness and 3 falls, worse when turning and in the dark. I suspected a cardiac cause, but Holter, echo and lying/standing BP were normal and cardiology found no arrhythmia. On re-examining him he has a wide-based gait, cannot tandem walk, and has mild dysarthria and past-pointing on the left. CT brain normal. Alcohol 2 standard drinks a week. No headache or vomiting. Gradually worse over the months.

Dr Shirin Moradi
note: Slowly progressive cerebellar signs with a normal CT after cardiac causes are excluded; hard because the falls were first worked up as cardiac.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mr Patrick Rourke, 42, had HFE gene testing after his brother was diagnosed with haemochromatosis: he is C282Y/H63D compound heterozygous. Ferritin 340, transferrin saturation 48%, LFTs normal. He is asymptomatic, with no joint pain or fatigue, and drinks about 10 standard drinks a week. I would appreciate advice on whether venesection or monitoring is needed, and on screening his children.

Regards,
Dr Tanvir Ahmed
note: Compound heterozygous HFE with mildly raised iron indices and normal LFTs; low-risk advice referral.

text:
Dear Respiratory Clinic,

Re: Maureen Callaghan, 68

Maureen has moderate COPD and I would value your advice on her inhalers, as she finds her Breezhaler device fiddly and wonders whether a combination inhaler would be simpler. Her last exacerbation was 18 months ago. When I asked about her cough she mentioned that over the past month she has coughed up blood-streaked sputum several times, and her weight is down 6 kg since autumn. Ex-smoker of 50 pack-years. CXR ordered.

Kind regards,
Dr Angus Fenwick
note: Haemoptysis and weight loss in a heavy ex-smoker are suspected lung cancer; hard because they are buried in an inhaler-device query.

text:
Re: Fiona Gallagher, 52

Fiona had a CT coronary calcium score arranged privately: score 38 (65th percentile), with mild non-obstructive plaque. She is asymptomatic, walks daily and is a non-smoker. BP 128/80, LDL 3.6. I have started rosuvastatin 10 mg. She would like a cardiologist to explain the result and advise whether any further testing is needed, as her friend was told she needed an angiogram for a similar score.

Dr Owen Leckie
note: Low calcium score in an asymptomatic woman already on a statin; explanation and advice only.

text:
Dear Neurologist,

Ms Ruth Ellery, 50, has 18 months of involuntary turning of her head to the right, with neck pulling and pain, worse when stressed or walking. Touching her chin (a 'sensory trick') helps. Exam otherwise normal. Not on dopamine-blocking drugs. She has difficulty driving and is reducing her hours as a receptionist. Physio has not helped. Would appreciate assessment and consideration of botulinum toxin.

Regards,
Dr Owen Clarke
note: Cervical dystonia causing pain and work impact but not deteriorating quickly.

text:
Re: Marion Gillespie, 59

Five months of painful white lacy patches inside both cheeks and erosions on the gums, making spicy and acidic foods difficult. She also has itchy violaceous papules on both wrists. Her dentist's biopsy confirmed lichen planus. Topical steroid paste has given partial relief only. Weight stable. Would appreciate management advice and consideration of systemic therapy.

Dr Fergus Lyall
note: Symptomatic erosive oral lichen planus failing topical therapy; painful but not rapidly deteriorating.

text:
Re: Kenji Morimoto, 47

Chest discomfort sometimes. ECG normal. Please review and advise. He is worried about it and his wife wants it checked. No other details available.

PMH: reflux, gout.
Meds: allopurinol 300 mg, pantoprazole 20 mg prn.
Allergies: nil known.
Social: non-smoker, works as a chef, married with two children.
Family history: not recorded.

Thank you,
Dr Anne-Marie Doucet
note: Intermittent chest discomfort with a normal ECG and no exertional or other red-flag features stated, so routine by default; hard because character, triggers and duration are all missing.

text:
Re: Alana Murphy, 24

Migraine with aura since 15, 3 to 4 attacks a year, well controlled with ibuprofen and rizatriptan. Normal exam. She was on the combined pill until I raised concerns about aura and stroke risk; we have switched her to a progestogen-only option. She would like a neurologist's view on long-term management and whether any preventive is needed.

Dr Hugo Laurent
note: Infrequent, well-controlled migraine with aura; contraception already adjusted.

text:
Re: Fatima Siddiqui, 45

Persistent dyspepsia with H. pylori infection that has failed two eradication courses (triple therapy, then a bismuth-based quadruple regimen); urea breath test still positive last month. Epigastric discomfort after meals, but no weight loss, vomiting, dysphagia or anaemia (Hb 132). Would appreciate gastroscopy with biopsy for culture and sensitivities, and advice on further eradication.

Dr Alexandre Dubois
note: Refractory H. pylori with ongoing symptoms and no alarm features.

text:
Re: Daniel Ferreira, 39

Felt a 'kick' in his left heel playing squash 5 days ago. Unable to push off and walking flat-footed. Positive Simmonds' test with a palpable gap 4 cm above the insertion. Ultrasound: complete Achilles tendon rupture, 18 mm gap in plantarflexion. He has been placed in a boot with heel wedges. Fit, non-smoker, no steroid or fluoroquinolone use. Would appreciate assessment for operative versus non-operative management.

Dr Wei Zhang
note: Acute complete Achilles rupture where the management decision is time-critical.

text:
Dear Neurology,

Re: Elijah Brookes, 26

Tourette syndrome diagnosed in childhood under paediatric neurology. Mild motor tics (blinking, shoulder shrugging) and occasional throat clearing, stable for years. He manages well and works as a graphic designer. He was previously on clonidine, stopped at 18. He has moved from Adelaide and would like an adult neurologist to discuss whether behavioural therapy (CBIT) might help.

Dr Sienna Walsh
note: Mild, long-standing stable tics; transfer of care and treatment options.

text:
Dear Dr,

URGENT review please.

Re: Doreen Walsh, 66

Doreen had a 5 mm solid nodule in the left lower lobe on CT in 2023. Repeat CT this month shows it unchanged in size and appearance over 2 years. Never smoker, asymptomatic, weight stable. She is anxious because her neighbour was recently diagnosed with lung cancer and she wants to see a specialist as soon as possible.

Dr Craig Fenner
note: A small solid nodule stable for 2 years in a never smoker is low risk and routine; hard because the GP requests urgent review.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Mr Callum Reyes, 32, has an LDL of 6.1 mmol/L, untreated. His father had an MI at 41. He has Achilles tendon xanthomata and a Dutch Lipid Clinic score of 9 (definite familial hypercholesterolaemia). He is asymptomatic, a non-smoker and active. I have started rosuvastatin 20 mg. I'd appreciate confirmation of the diagnosis, genetic testing and advice on cascade screening for his two children.

Regards,
Dr Yusuf Kaya
note: Asymptomatic familial hypercholesterolaemia already on treatment; diagnosis and family screening, no active cardiac disease.

text:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Mr Kevin O'Driscoll, 71, worked as a plumber with asbestos lagging in the 1970s. A CT abdomen for kidney stones incidentally showed calcified bilateral pleural plaques. He is a former smoker, quit in 1995. He is asymptomatic, with normal spirometry and no effusion or lung mass. He has asked about his risk and about any compensation process.

Regards,
Dr Fiona Lacey
note: Benign pleural plaques in an asymptomatic man with normal lung function.

text:
Dear Gastroenterology,

Ms Olivia Brandt, 40, was diagnosed with coeliac disease in 2019 and has followed a strict gluten-free diet since. Her tTG has normalised and she is asymptomatic with normal Hb, ferritin and vitamin D. She would like to know whether she needs a repeat biopsy to confirm healing, and advice on bone density testing and long-term follow-up.

Kind regards,
Dr Hamish Carlisle
note: Well-controlled coeliac disease; follow-up planning questions only.

text:
Re: Claire Donnelly, 49

Intermittent burning pain between the 3rd and 4th toes of the left foot for a year, mainly when she wears heels to work functions, settling when she takes her shoes off. Ultrasound: 6 mm Morton's neuroma. A metatarsal pad and wider shoes from her podiatrist have helped considerably. She would like to know about longer-term options, including injection or surgery.

Dr Hugh Bannerman
note: Morton's neuroma largely controlled with footwear changes; minimal dysfunction.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mr Luca Romano, 33, a baker for 8 years, has had wheeze, chest tightness and a runny nose at work for 18 months, improving noticeably on weekends and during his holidays. Serial peak flows show a 25% drop on work days. Spirometry: mild obstruction with significant bronchodilator reversibility. Started on budesonide/formoterol with partial benefit. Suspect occupational asthma due to flour; he is worried about his job.

Regards,
Dr Hannah Kwok
note: Suspected occupational asthma needs specialist confirmation within months; symptomatic but not deteriorating quickly.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Gordon Pyke, 52

Gordon has had a dry cough for 5 months, worse after meals and on lying down, with frequent throat clearing and a sour taste in the mornings. I suspected asthma, but spirometry with bronchodilator was normal and an 8-week trial of inhaled fluticasone made no difference. CXR normal. Non-smoker, not on an ACE inhibitor. Heartburn twice a week. Pantoprazole started 4 weeks ago with some improvement. No weight loss, dysphagia or haemoptysis. Would appreciate gastroscopy and advice on reflux management.

Dr Lisa Arkwright
note: Chronic cough attributed to reflux after asthma is excluded, without alarm features, is semi-urgent gastroenterology; hard because the cough and inhaler trial point to respiratory.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Mrs Gina Taverner, 52, administration officer, has had left lateral elbow pain for 10 months consistent with lateral epicondylitis. With a physio-guided loading program and a counterforce brace it has improved by about two thirds, and she now gets mild pain only when lifting a full kettle. No time off work. She would like an opinion on whether a PRP or other injection would speed things up.

Regards,
Dr Amos Kirkland
note: Improving tennis elbow with mild residual pain and no work impact.

text:
Dear Dr,

No rush with this one, I suspect it's just reflux. Mr Hector Ramos, 58, has had trouble swallowing for 6 weeks, with food sticking at the lower chest, and it is getting worse; he now cuts food very small and sometimes regurgitates it. He thinks he has lost some weight, and our scales show 6 kg down since June. Smoker. Started esomeprazole 40 mg a fortnight ago without benefit.

Thanks,
Dr Kate Dalziel
note: Progressive dysphagia with weight loss in a smoker is a cancer red flag; hard because the GP says 'no rush' and frames it as reflux.

text:
Re: Paige Holloway, 20

An X-ray of the left knee after a minor netball knock showed a 2 cm pedunculated bony outgrowth from the distal femoral metaphysis pointing away from the joint, reported as a typical osteochondroma. It is painless, has not changed in size that she has noticed, and she has no other lumps. The knock has fully settled. She would like to know whether it needs removal or monitoring.

Dr Sean O'Rourke
note: Painless incidental osteochondroma with typical features in a young adult.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Stuart Llewellyn, 48, electrician. 9 months of right shoulder pain, worse with overhead work, with a painful arc from 70 to 120 degrees and night pain lying on that side. Ultrasound: supraspinatus tendinopathy with a partial-thickness bursal-side tear and subacromial bursitis. A subacromial injection in April helped for 6 weeks only, and he has done 4 months of physio. He is on light duties and his employer wants a plan. No neck symptoms.

Thanks,
Dr Ingrid Solberg
note: Rotator cuff tendinopathy with partial tear failing conservative care and limiting work; not a condition likely to deteriorate quickly.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Mrs Shirley Marsh, 64, has had 4 months of watery diarrhoea 5 to 6 times a day, sometimes waking her at night, without blood or weight loss. She started sertraline 6 months ago and has been on lansoprazole for years. Calprotectin 95. Coeliac serology, TFTs and stool PCR negative; Hb normal. Stopping caffeine made no difference. It is restricting her outings with her grandchildren. Suspect microscopic colitis; would appreciate colonoscopy with biopsies.

Regards,
Dr Mia Lawson
note: Chronic watery diarrhoea suggestive of microscopic colitis, disabling but without bleeding, anaemia or weight loss.

text:
Re: Yvette Barnes, 56

Yvette has kept pigeons for 15 years. Over 6 months she has developed a dry cough and mild breathlessness on hills, with episodes of fever and aches after cleaning the loft. CT chest: centrilobular ground-glass nodules and mosaic attenuation. Spirometry mildly restrictive, gas transfer 68%. SpO2 97%. Avian precipitins sent. Suspect hypersensitivity pneumonitis; she is reluctant to part with the birds.

Dr Clive Ashcombe
note: Suspected hypersensitivity pneumonitis with mild impairment; needs specialist diagnosis and antigen-avoidance advice within months.

text:
Dear Cardiology / Respiratory,

Re: Neil Hargraves, 70

Neil has become gradually more breathless over a year, now stopping after 200 m. Ex-smoker (40 pack-years). I first wondered about his heart, but echo shows normal LV and valve function and NT-proBNP is normal. Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 55% predicted, with no significant reversibility. CXR: hyperinflation. Tiotropium started 6 weeks ago with modest improvement. No haemoptysis or weight loss. I'd appreciate assessment and advice on optimising treatment.

Dr Kate Wexford
note: Newly diagnosed moderate COPD with progressive breathlessness after cardiac causes are excluded is semi-urgent respiratory; hard because the letter is addressed to cardiology as well.

text:
Re: Laila Mansour, 35

Long-standing intermittent constipation since childhood, with bowels open every 2 to 3 days, managed with Movicol. No bleeding, weight loss or change in pattern. FBC, TFTs, calcium and coeliac serology normal. No family history of bowel disease. Diet includes plenty of fibre. She would like a specialist to discuss longer-term options and whether she needs any tests.

Dr Benjamin Yeo
note: Lifelong stable constipation with normal bloods and no alarm features.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mrs Edna Whitlock, 82, has permanent AF diagnosed in 2016, on apixaban 2.5 mg bd and diltiazem CD 180 mg. Resting rate 72, no breathlessness beyond her baseline, no falls and no bleeding. Echo 2023: normal LV function, moderately dilated atria. She was last seen by cardiology 5 years ago. Her family have asked for a specialist check to make sure her treatment is still right. Renal function stable, eGFR 48.

Kind regards,
Dr Celeste Moreau
note: Long-standing, well-controlled permanent AF; the family requested a review with no change in clinical status.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mr Ronald Fairweather, 79, widower living alone. Over the last 3 weeks he has become breathless walking to his letterbox and has twice nearly blacked out climbing the stairs at his daughter's house. He also gets tightness in his chest on exertion. On examination there is a harsh ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids, a slow-rising pulse and a soft S2. No murmur was documented at his check-up in 2023. ECG: LVH with strain. Echo requested, but the local wait is 6 weeks.

Kind regards,
Dr Elise Varnham
note: Suspected severe aortic stenosis with exertional presyncope, angina and breathlessness.

text:
Re: Warren Bligh, 51

A 2 cm cyst on the upper back for 5 years, with a central punctum and an occasional cheesy, smelly discharge. It has never been infected or painful and has not changed in size recently. No other lumps. He would like it removed because it catches on his backpack straps. Otherwise well, on no anticoagulants.

Dr Kirsten Moller
note: Uncomplicated epidermoid cyst; minor nuisance only.

text:
Cardiology outpatients

Jasmine Okoro, 38, has mitral valve prolapse with trivial MR on echo in 2019. She has occasional fleeting chest twinges unrelated to exertion, with no palpitations, syncope or breathlessness. Exam: mid-systolic click, no murmur. ECG normal. She would like to know whether she needs repeat imaging and whether there are any restrictions on exercise, as she has started CrossFit.

Dr Lionel Baptiste
note: Mitral valve prolapse with trivial MR and no concerning symptoms; surveillance advice only.

text:
Dear Orthopaedics / Neurology,

Re: Bianca Leone, 40

Six weeks of mid-back ache, and more recently both legs feel numb and 'like walking on cotton wool', and she has to rush to the toilet to pass urine. She initially put it down to her back after the gym. Exam: sensory level around T10, brisk knee and ankle reflexes, bilateral upgoing plantars and mild leg weakness. Upper limbs normal. Twelve months ago she had an episode of blurred vision in the right eye that settled by itself. MRI is booked for next week.

Dr Aiden Price
note: Progressive myelopathy with upper motor neuron signs and possible prior optic neuritis needs urgent neurology (ED if rapidly worsening); hard because it is framed as back pain and also addressed to orthopaedics.

text:
Dear Respiratory Clinic,

Ms Ebony Clarke, 25, a keen distance runner, gets chest tightness and cough a few minutes after hard runs in cold weather, settling within half an hour. Two puffs of salbutamol before running prevent it. Resting spirometry normal. No symptoms at other times. She is training for a marathon and would like a specialist opinion on whether anything more is needed.

Kind regards,
Dr Mitchell Avery
note: Mild exercise-induced bronchoconstriction well controlled with pre-exercise reliever.

text:
Dear Dermatologist,

Mr Clive Hartnett, 74, a retired farmer who is bald, has a firm pink-red nodule on the vertex of his scalp that appeared over 6 weeks, now 14 mm, and has bled twice onto his hat. It is non-pigmented and dome-shaped, with irregular vessels on dermoscopy. He has had several SCCs and BCCs excised in the past. I am concerned about amelanotic nodular melanoma or an aggressive SCC. Could he please be seen urgently. No palpable cervical nodes.

Dr Tara Quinlan
note: Rapidly growing bleeding scalp nodule: suspected nodular melanoma or SCC; the GP's urgent request matches.

text:
Dear Respiratory / Cardiology,

Re: Priya Raghunathan, 61

I initially treated Priya for late-onset asthma: 5 weeks of wheeze and breathlessness, with little response to budesonide/formoterol. On review she now describes needing to sleep propped up and waking at night gasping, with swollen ankles. Spirometry showed no reversibility. NT-proBNP 2,850. CXR: cardiomegaly, upper lobe diversion and Kerley B lines. ECG: sinus tachycardia 104, poor R wave progression. Non-smoker. I now think this is cardiac.

Dr Michael Strand
note: Wheeze from new heart failure (orthopnoea, PND, oedema, raised NT-proBNP, CXR changes) is urgent cardiology; hard because it was presented as asthma and addressed to two services.

text:
Dear Orthopaedic Clinic,

Mr Rhys Callaghan, 41, separated his right AC joint (grade II) mountain biking 3 years ago, managed in a sling. He has a visible bump over the joint and an occasional ache after bench press, but full range of movement, full strength and no night pain. X-ray: mild AC joint arthritis with slight elevation of the clavicle. He would like advice about whether anything can be done about the bump and the ache.

Regards,
Dr Mei Lin Ho
note: Old AC joint injury with mild arthritis and cosmetic concern; minimal dysfunction.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mrs Valerie Thompson, 66, has many flat brown spots on the backs of her hands and face that have accumulated over decades of gardening. They are uniform in colour, with typical solar lentigo features on dermoscopy, and none has changed recently. She is bothered by their appearance and would like advice about laser treatment, along with reassurance.

Regards,
Dr Robert Ince
note: Benign solar lentigines with a cosmetic concern.

text:
Re: Monique Ferrier, 46

Monique had Guillain-Barre syndrome 2 years ago, treated with IVIg at your hospital, and was discharged from follow-up after 6 months. She now walks unaided and is back at work. She has residual mild fatigue and occasional tingling in her toes, unchanged for a year. Exam: absent ankle jerks, otherwise normal. She has been offered a flu vaccine and wants specialist advice about vaccine safety and her residual symptoms.

Dr Gavin Moss
note: Stable recovery after GBS with minor residual symptoms; advice only.

text:
Re: Jordan Whitlam, 29

Third episode of pericarditis in 2 years. The latest, 5 weeks ago, was treated with ibuprofen and colchicine; pain has resolved, CRP is back to 4, and echo shows no effusion. He remains on colchicine 500 mcg bd. Each recurrence has followed tapering of treatment and has cost him time off work as an apprentice electrician. I would value advice on duration of therapy and whether further investigation is needed for recurrent pericarditis.

Dr Simone Garrick
note: Recurrent pericarditis, currently settled on colchicine; needs specialist planning but is not acutely unwell.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Florence Ng, 67

Florence has 4 weeks of drooping of the left eyelid and double vision, both worse in the evening and after reading, and recently some difficulty chewing tough meat by the end of a meal. No breathing difficulty. Exam: left ptosis worsening after sustained upgaze, variable diplopia, mild neck flexion weakness. An ice pack test improved the ptosis. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies sent. Grateful for an urgent review. I have advised her to go to ED if she has trouble swallowing or breathing.

Dr Joseph Amato
note: Suspected myasthenia gravis with early bulbar symptoms can deteriorate quickly; the GP's urgent request matches.

text:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Mrs Beatrice Lunn, 78, was found to be anaemic on bloods for fatigue: Hb 92, MCV 71, ferritin 6. She has no abdominal symptoms, normal bowel habit and no visible bleeding, and her weight is stable. No NSAIDs or anticoagulants, and her diet is adequate. Coeliac serology negative, urinalysis normal. Her last bowel screening test was 5 years ago (negative). I have started oral iron. Would appreciate gastroscopy and colonoscopy.

Kind regards,
Dr Owen Mackie
note: Unexplained iron deficiency anaemia in an older woman requires urgent upper and lower endoscopy even without GI symptoms.

text:
Re: Ernest Kowal, 74

Two years of bilateral buttock and leg aching on walking, now after 200 m, relieved by sitting or leaning on a shopping trolley. Foot pulses palpable, ABI 1.05 bilaterally. Neurological exam normal at rest. MRI: severe central canal stenosis at L3/4 and L4/5. An epidural injection 6 months ago helped briefly. He has given up golf and his daily walk. Bladder and bowel fine. Would value a surgical opinion.

Dr Annabel Cross
note: Neurogenic claudication from lumbar stenosis limiting walking, with no progressive deficit.

text:
Dear Cardio-oncology / Cardiology,

Mrs Leanne Petrovic, 48, completed adjuvant doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide for breast cancer in June. Her surveillance echo shows LVEF has fallen from 62% before chemotherapy to 48%, with GLS -15%. She feels well, with no breathlessness, oedema or palpitations and is back at work part time. BP 126/78. I have started ramipril 2.5 mg. Her oncologist suggested cardiology review for cardiomyopathy management.

Kind regards,
Dr Bronwyn Tate
note: Asymptomatic anthracycline-related LV dysfunction already started on treatment; needs review within months.

text:
Re: Thanh Nguyen, 47

Mild flaking and redness of the eyebrows, nasolabial folds and scalp for years, flaring in winter. Ketoconazole shampoo and occasional hydrocortisone cream help, but it returns when he stops. He works as an electrician and is otherwise well. No hair loss and no other skin problems. He would like longer-term advice on keeping it under control.

Dr Sarah Pemberton-Hill
note: Mild seborrhoeic dermatitis controlled with simple measures.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mr Clifford Owens, 58, has had 8 months of numbness and burning over the outer right thigh, worse after long periods standing and with his work belt. Exam: patch of reduced sensation over the anterolateral thigh, normal power and reflexes, no back pain. HbA1c 6.0. His weight is up 10 kg this year. Symptoms are stable and bearable. He would like confirmation of the diagnosis.

Regards,
Dr Tess Harper
note: Meralgia paraesthetica: stable, purely sensory and benign.

text:
Dear Dr,

Please see urgently, she is very distressed.

Re: Alexis Moran, 24

Alexis has patchy hair loss that began 3 months ago and has spread to several smooth, round patches now covering about 30% of her scalp, with exclamation-mark hairs at the margins. Eyebrows and nails are normal. TFTs, FBC and ferritin normal. Intralesional steroid is not available in my practice and potent topical steroid has not helped. She is avoiding work and social events.

Dr Natasha Ivers
note: Extensive alopecia areata failing topical treatment is distressing but not dangerous, so semi-urgent; hard because the GP asks for urgent review.

text:
Re: Jack Mbatha, 19

Jack had asthma as a child but has not needed a puffer since he was 12. He is applying to join the Army, and Defence Recruiting has asked for specialist confirmation of his current asthma status. Spirometry with bronchodilator today was normal. He runs 10 km twice a week without symptoms, has no hay fever, and uses no inhalers.

Dr Lauren Petrie
note: Childhood asthma now in remission; paperwork for recruitment.

text:
Re: Peter Lindgren-Shaw, 64

Ex-smoker, 30 pack-years. A 9 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe found on CT in July has grown to 14 mm on the 3-month follow-up CT, with new lobulated margins. No lymphadenopathy. Asymptomatic, weight stable, FEV1 85% predicted. On no anticoagulants. Mother had lung cancer at 70. Please see urgently for further work-up.

Dr Lorraine Batty
note: An enlarging solid nodule in an ex-smoker is suspected lung cancer; the GP's urgent request matches.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Kenneth Hollow, 71

Kenneth has moderate bilateral knee osteoarthritis, left worse than right, managed with paracetamol and a knee brace. He would like to discuss options as it is limiting his walks. Of more concern, he has had 6 weeks of aching in the right upper arm that wakes him at night, and he has lost 5 kg without trying. He had prostate cancer treated with radiotherapy in 2019. X-ray right humerus last week: lytic lesion in the proximal shaft. PSA pending.

Kind regards,
Dr Philippa Grant
note: Night pain, weight loss and a lytic humeral lesion after prostate cancer suggest metastasis; hard because the letter opens as a knee OA referral.

text:
Dear Dermatologist,

Mr Gordon Fairclough, 63, has noticed increasing numbers of small bright red spots on his chest and abdomen over the last 10 years. They are 1 to 3 mm, dome-shaped and asymptomatic, consistent with cherry angiomas. FBC, LFTs and platelets are normal. He read online that they can be a sign of cancer and would like reassurance from a specialist.

Kind regards,
Dr Alana Brooks
note: Benign cherry angiomas with normal bloods; reassurance only.

text:
Re: Ryan Tomkins, 24

Isolated raised bilirubin found on bloods for a sports medical: total bilirubin 32, unconjugated, rising to 41 after a weekend of fasting during exams. Mild intermittent yellowing of his eyes noted by his mother. ALT, ALP, GGT, albumin, FBC and reticulocytes normal; no haemolysis. Asymptomatic, no alcohol excess. I suspect Gilbert's syndrome. He would like this confirmed before his medical is finalised.

Dr Imogen Ravel
note: Probable Gilbert's syndrome with otherwise normal tests; benign.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Imogen Fairley, 29

Imogen has around 60 naevi, fair skin and a grandmother who had melanoma. She would like regular full-body skin checks and advice on mole mapping, and most of her naevi look benign on dermoscopy today. However, her partner has noticed that one on the back of her left calf has become larger and darker since winter. It measures 9 mm, is asymmetric with an irregular border and two shades of brown, and shows an atypical network on dermoscopy.

Kind regards,
Dr Brendan Oakes
note: A changing, asymmetric 9 mm calf naevus with atypical dermoscopy is suspicious for melanoma; hard because it is buried in a request for skin surveillance.

text:
Re: Benjamin Hogg, 41

Episodic cluster headache since his 20s, with bouts every 1 to 2 years. The current bout started 3 weeks ago: 1 to 2 attacks nightly of severe right orbital pain with tearing and nasal blockage, lasting 45 minutes. High-flow oxygen helps; sumatriptan injections are limited by PBS quantity. Verapamil started at 80 mg tds; baseline ECG normal. Previous MRI normal. Would appreciate help with preventive management for this and future bouts.

Dr Hana Kimura
note: Known episodic cluster headache in an active bout, partly controlled, with no new features.

text:
Dear Dermatology,

Ms Catherine Obi, 33, a theatre nurse, has had hand dermatitis for 9 months with fissuring, vesicles and pain on the palms and fingers, worse with frequent handwashing and gloves. Potent topical steroid, barrier creams and cotton glove liners have not controlled it, and she has had two weeks off work this month. Occupational health has suggested patch testing to look for an allergen such as rubber accelerators.

Regards,
Dr Jasper Hollins
note: Severe occupational hand dermatitis failing treatment and causing time off work.

text:
Re: Faisal Rahman, 44

Pulmonary sarcoidosis diagnosed in 2019 in Sydney, treated with prednisolone for a year, and off treatment and in remission for 4 years. CXR now shows only minor residual hilar prominence, and spirometry and gas transfer are normal. Asymptomatic. He has moved here and would like his care transferred and advice on how often he needs monitoring.

Dr Josie Halloran
note: Sarcoidosis in remission; transfer of care for monitoring.

text:
Re: Darcy McIntyre, 44

Darcy had a single generalised seizure 3 years ago during alcohol withdrawal, investigated at the time with a normal MRI and EEG. He has been abstinent since, with no further events, and is not on antiseizure medication. Neurological exam normal. He is applying for a heavy vehicle licence and the licensing authority has asked for a specialist report on his fitness to drive.

Dr Paula Wren
note: Single provoked seizure years ago with no recurrence; fitness-to-drive paperwork only.

Re: Margot Ainsley, 57

An ultrasound done for gallstone symptoms (now resolved) showed a 3.5 cm simple hepatic cyst: thin-walled, no septations or solid components. LFTs and liver ultrasound otherwise normal, no other lesions. No history of travel or hydatid exposure. She is asymptomatic but anxious and would like a specialist explanation. Non-urgent review is fine, thank you.

Dr Petra Hollingsworth
note: Simple hepatic cyst with no concerning features; the GP's non-urgent request matches.

Re: Mia Castellanos, 26

Excessive underarm sweating since her teens, stable over many years. Aluminium chloride antiperspirant gives partial benefit. No night sweats, weight loss or generalised sweating, and thyroid function is normal. It is embarrassing at work, where she wears dark tops and carries spare shirts, but she manages. She would like to discuss botulinum toxin or other options.

Dr Oliver Kemp
note: Primary focal hyperhidrosis without systemic features; quality-of-life concern only.

text:
Dear Neurology / Orthopaedics,

Mrs Lorraine Fitzpatrick, 58, has had numbness and tingling in the right thumb, index and middle fingers for 8 months, worse at night and when driving, with some neck stiffness. I wondered about cervical radiculopathy, but there is no arm pain, reflexes are normal and MRI cervical spine shows only mild age-related change without foraminal stenosis. Phalen's and Tinel's are positive at the wrist. Nerve conduction: moderate right median neuropathy at the wrist. Splinting has not helped. Grip mildly weak, no wasting.

Dr Patrick Hendry
note: Confirmed moderate carpal tunnel syndrome failing splinting is a semi-urgent surgical (hand) referral; hard because it is also addressed to neurology and raises an excluded cervical cause.

Dear Dr,

Re: Wendy Sorensen, 63

Wendy has had intermittent mild right groin ache for 18 months, mainly after gardening. She walks 4 km daily, sleeps well and needs paracetamol once or twice a week. Hip internal rotation is slightly reduced. X-ray: mild joint space narrowing. She would like a specialist opinion because her sister recently had a hip replaced and she wants to know whether she is heading the same way.

Kind regards,
Dr Bruno Esposito
note: Mild hip OA with minimal pain and preserved function.
